jurisdiction.name: San Francisco
jurisdiction.notes: City and County of San Francisco. Most food-business permits are coordinated through the Office of Small Business's Permit Center at 49 South Van Ness. The Mission has an Alcoholic Beverage Special Use District restricting new bar licenses.

permits.name: San Francisco Business Registration Certificate
permits.issuing_agency: SF Office of the Treasurer & Tax Collector
permits.notes: Required within 30 days of starting business in SF; the registration year runs April 1 to March 31 and renewal is due by the last day of February. Fee is tiered by SF gross receipts (e.g. $55 up to $100k, $95 up to $250k, $625 at $1–1.5M for 2026–27, each plus a $4 state fee). Every other city department asks for your Business Account Number (BAN), so do this immediately after forming the entity.

permits.name: Fictitious Business Name (DBA) statement
permits.issuing_agency: SF Office of the County Clerk
permits.notes: Needed if the public-facing name differs from the legal entity name (almost always true for a restaurant or bar). Register with the Tax Collector first, file the FBN statement with the County Clerk in person (photo ID) or by mail, then publish in a court-approved newspaper once a week for four weeks and file proof of publication within 45 days. Banks and ABC want the filed statement.

permits.name: Planning Department zoning referral / change of use review
permits.notes: A building permit with a change of use (e.g. retail → restaurant) is routed to Planning for zoning review, neighborhood notification (Section 311/312) where required, and formula-retail checks. Over-the-counter if the use is principally permitted in the zoning district and no notification is triggered; several months if a neighborhood notification or discretionary review is filed.
permits.stall_risk: Discretionary Review requests from neighbors can add 3–6 months. Check the Property Information Map for the zoning district and any Special Use District before signing the lease.

permits.name: Conditional Use Authorization (bar / nightlife use)
permits.notes: Bars (ABC Types 42/48) and nightclubs are conditional uses in most Neighborhood Commercial districts and require a Planning Commission hearing with 300-foot mailed notice and a posted notice, followed by a 30-day appeal period. A no-construction CUA was $2,747 on the 2023–24 schedule and is CPI-adjusted each year (about $3,150 now); fees rise with construction cost, and new storefront businesses may qualify for First Year Free fee waivers. In the Mission Alcoholic Beverage Special Use District new bar uses are generally prohibited unless an existing license is transferred within the district; restaurants serving alcohol incidental to meals usually skip this step.
permits.stall_risk: This is the critical path for any bar: 6–10 months including pre-application community meeting, environmental review, and hearing scheduling. File the CUA before or in parallel with the lease negotiation, with a contingency clause.

permits.name: Building permit (tenant improvements / change of occupancy)
permits.notes: Kitchen build-outs, hoods, restrooms, ADA upgrades and any change of occupancy need a DBI permit with plans stamped by an architect. Since September 14, 2026 most over-the-counter permits are filed only through the PermitSF portal; full plan review with Planning, Fire, Public Health and PUC routing takes 2–4 months. Fees are a percentage of construction valuation. Separate electrical, plumbing and mechanical permits are pulled by licensed subcontractors.
permits.stall_risk: Incomplete plan sets bounce between departments. Hire an architect who has done SF restaurants and submit the DPH plan check at the same time.

permits.name: Public Health plan check (new or remodeled food facility)
permits.issuing_agency: SF Department of Public Health – Environmental Health Branch
permits.notes: Any new food facility or remodel affecting the kitchen needs DPH approval of plans, finishes, equipment and menu; make sure 'health' is a routing station on the DBI application. FY2026–27 flat fees: $828 (small remodel, 3 hrs), $1,241 (bar/prepackaged, 4.5 hrs), $2,207 (new restaurant, 8 hrs), with extra review at $276/hr. After approval, schedule a pre-final inspection at ~80% complete and a final inspection, booking each with your plan reviewer at least two weeks ahead.

permits.name: Health Permit to Operate a food facility
permits.issuing_agency: SF Department of Public Health – Environmental Health Branch
permits.notes: Apply online at least one month before opening with your BAN, Location ID (LIN) and federal tax ID; the permit is issued after the final inspection confirms the facility matches the approved plans and a certified food safety manager is on staff. FY2026–27 schedule: $470 Permit to Operate application (includes initial inspection) and $0 annual license fee for restaurants and bars for 2026–28; reinspections are $276/hr. A change of ownership or entity type (e.g. sole proprietor to LLC) needs a new permit, and you cannot serve the public before it is issued.
permits.stall_risk: Failed pre-opening inspections (missing hand sinks, unsealed surfaces, no hot water) push openings by 2–3 weeks. Walk the space against the DPH checklist a week before the inspection.

permits.name: Fire Department permit (place of assembly / commercial kitchen hood)
permits.issuing_agency: SF Fire Department – Bureau of Fire Prevention
permits.notes: Occupant loads of 50+ need a Place of Assembly permit ($446 at the SFFD Permit Center, 49 South Van Ness Suite 560; packets accepted until 4:30 pm) and a posted occupancy sign; the Entertainment Commission also requires this permit for venues of 50+. Commercial cooking hoods need a suppression-system plan review and inspection routed with the building permit. Schedule the final fire inspection before the DPH pre-opening inspection.

permits.name: Fats, Oils & Grease (FOG) program registration / grease interceptor
permits.issuing_agency: SF Public Utilities Commission – Wastewater Enterprise
permits.notes: Under the FOG Control Ordinance every food service establishment that cooks must install grease-capturing equipment; SFPUC inspectors assign a Discharger Category (1–3) that dictates the device type, and new restaurants must install it before opening. Submitting the Installation Verification Form earns a 14.2% reduction on the sewer portion of your bill. An undersized or missing interceptor is a common reason DBI withholds final sign-off.

permits.name: Sign permit (exterior business signage)
permits.issuing_agency: SF Planning Department + Department of Building Inspection
permits.notes: New or replaced exterior signs, awnings with text, and illuminated signs need a sign permit reviewed by Planning for size/illumination rules and issued by DBI. Historic districts and Article 10/11 buildings take longer. Window vinyl under the size threshold is usually exempt.

permits.name: Limited Live Performance (LLP) permit
permits.notes: For restaurants, cafes and bars where live performance is a secondary, ongoing use that ends by 10 or 11 pm (depending on zoning) in a performance area of 200 sq ft or less. Process: online application, intake meeting, $612 fee (2026–27), neighbor outreach plus a yellow notice posted for 30 days, then an Entertainment Commission hearing (1st and 3rd Tuesdays). Later shows, DJs or dancing need the Place of Entertainment permit instead.

permits.name: Place of Entertainment (POE) permit
permits.notes: Required when entertainment is a primary use (live music venue, nightclub, DJs, dancing) or shows run until 2 am. Email the Deputy Director to confirm zoning eligibility before applying; new businesses need a lease or temporary liquor license, and venues of 50+ need the SFFD Place of Assembly permit. $2,708 application fee (2026–27) plus other departments' inspection fees, Police and Planning review, a 30-day posted notice and a Commission hearing.
permits.stall_risk: Sound complaints from upstairs residents are the main reason POE permits are conditioned or denied; commission an acoustic report and soundproofing plan before the hearing.

permits.name: Extended Hours Premises permit (open between 2 am and 6 am)
permits.notes: Any business hosting entertainment or serving food and non-alcoholic drinks to the public between 2 am and 6 am needs this permit. Same path as the POE: eligibility email, intake meeting, $2,708 application fee (2026–27), Police/Planning referral, 30-day posted notice and Commission hearing. Alcohol service must still stop at 2 am under state law.

permits.name: Shared Spaces permit (sidewalk tables / parklet)
permits.issuing_agency: SF Shared Spaces program (Public Works / SFMTA / Planning)
permits.notes: Since August 2025 small businesses no longer need a permit or fee for sidewalk tables, chairs or merchandise displays; they only register. Parking-lane parklets still need a Shared Spaces permit: 2026–27 one-time fees run $1,186 (public) to $3,559 (fixed commercial) for the first space plus $119–$2,373 per space per year, halved for businesses under $5M gross receipts and billed only after the permit is issued. Parklets need design review, an ADA path, and liability insurance naming the City.

permits.name: Transient Occupancy Tax (TOT) Certificate of Authority
permits.issuing_agency: SF Office of the Treasurer & Tax Collector
permits.notes: Hotels, motels and inns must hold a Certificate of Authority from the Treasurer & Tax Collector before collecting the 14% TOT; hotels in the Tourism Improvement District also owe a 2.25% (Zone 1) or 2.00% (Zone 2) assessment. TOT, TID and MED returns are filed monthly, including zero-rent months. Short-term rental hosts do not need a COA.

permits.name: Hotel Certificate of Occupancy / annual fire and housing inspection
permits.issuing_agency: SF Department of Building Inspection – Housing Inspection Services + SF Fire Department
permits.notes: Lodging uses need an R-1 occupancy certificate, fire alarm/sprinkler sign-off and recurring DBI housing inspections. The Hotel Conversion Ordinance restricts converting residential hotel rooms to tourist use; verify the room count on the DBI certificate before opening.

permits.name: Mobile Food Facility health permit (food truck / cart)
permits.issuing_agency: SF Department of Public Health – Environmental Health Branch
permits.notes: Covers plan review of the vehicle ($414 low-risk / $690 high-risk in 2026–27), a commissary agreement, the $470 permit application with initial inspection, and an SFFD inspection of the truck; the 2026–27 annual license fee for mobile food facilities is $0. Submit two sets of scaled drawings, interior/exterior photos and a menu describing preparation through the DPH portal. Trucks permitted by another California county still need SF DPH approval to operate in the city.

permits.name: Mobile Food Facility location permit (public right-of-way)
permits.issuing_agency: SF Public Works – Bureau of Street-Use & Mapping
permits.notes: Public Works permit for each street location, starting at $1,151 with half of the processing, notification and inspection fees due at application. You post a notice at the site for 10 days and notify everyone within 75 feet, followed by a 30-day comment period; unresolved objections go to a public hearing, otherwise you get a 90-day tentative approval. Final issuance needs the DPH health permit, fire certificate, DMV registration and $2M liability insurance naming the City; private lots go through Planning and DPH instead.
permits.stall_risk: Location permits are routinely appealed by nearby restaurants; apply for 2–3 candidate locations at once.
